utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Would the witness make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Andric. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you commence your evidence, Mr. Andric, I must draw your attention to a certain Rule of Procedure and Evidence here at the International Tribunal, that is, Rule 90(E). Under this Rule you may object to answering any question from Mr. Karadzic, the Prosecution, or even from the Judges if you believe that your answer might incriminate you in a criminal offence. In this context, "incriminate" means saying something that might amount to an admission of guilt for a criminal offence or saying something that might provide evidence that you might have committed a criminal offence. However, should you think that an answer might incriminate you and, as a consequence, you refuse to answer the question, I must let you know that the Tribunal has the power to compel you to answer the question. But in that situation, the Tribunal would ensure that your testimony compelled under such circumstances would not be used in any case that might be laid against you for any offence save and except the offence of giving false testimony. Do you understand what I have just told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Andric. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Excellencies. Welcome, Judge Lattanzi, Your Excellency. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Andric.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, did you give my Defence team a statement?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court 1D7813.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that statement of yours in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, both you and I should pause between question and answer and we should speak slowly so that everything can be recorded in the transcript and that the interpreters can interpret everything that we say. Did you read and sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please take a look at the last page now. Could the witness identify his signature. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did this statement faithfully reflect what you said to the Defence team in response to their questions?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to put the same questions to you today, would your answers basically be the same?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I'd like to tender this 92 ter package.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. There are eight exhibits and we would ask that they be added to our 65 ter list, as they were not -- we hadn't interviewed this witness as of the time we filed that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say "eight"?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct -- actually seven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Mr. Zec?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit them, but as to the photographs referred to in para 13 I would like to ask the accused to clarify with the witness when these pictures were taken and whether it -- and what part has been changed. We'll give the numbers for the statement as well as the associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the statement 65 ter 1D7813 will be Exhibit D3038, and the seven exhibits will be Exhibits D3039 through Exhibit D3045 respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I'm going to read out the summary of Mr. Novica Andric's statement in the English language. [In English] Novica Andric was born on 28th of May, 1962, in Kosovo village, Rogatica municipality. He finished his primary school in Rogatica and there he continued with secondary school for car mechanics, and then he finished the traffic and transport technical school in Gorazde. In 1983 he went to Kraljevo to do his military service in the JNA in a military traffic police unit. Novica Andric noticed that after the establishment of national parties things at the political, economic, social, and national level suddenly changed and the situation rapidly began to deteriorate. The SDA, Muslim party, was formed in the first half of 1990 and Mr. Andric recalls that the SDS was not formed until much later in early September concerning Rogatica municipality. The first illegal armed unit in the eastern part of Bosnia was formed in Pokrivenik, a Muslim-inhabited village, in late 1990 into early 1991. Many Serbs expected that this situation would be resolved; however, these hopes only lasted until the referendum on the secession of Bosnia and Herzegovina from Yugoslavia. After this referendum, nationalism increased and it was apparent to Mr. Novica Andric that Serbs, Croats, and Muslims could no longer live together in harmony. Many Muslims said that Bosnia belonged to them and that they were going to have it. In Rogatica there was a total distrust among the people, and as a precaution the Serbs started organising village guards at night using hunting weapons which they legally possessed. This was done because from the beginning of the second half of 1991 volleys from automatic weapons could often be heard from Muslim villages. Novica Andric joined the Serbian Territorial Defence around 20th of April, 1992, and was tasked with protecting the villages that faced the Muslim villages as these villages had armed very early and possessed all kind of infantry weapons. At around the same time the weapons of the former Rogatica Territorial Defence were distributed to the Territorial Defence. All the weapons kept -- were kept in the JNA depots for safety reasons. The Territorial Defence was not armed by the JNA, that merely stored their weapons in the depots. From the beginning of May 1992 there were constant provocations from the Muslim villages. They often fired at the Serbian homes using infantry weapons, anti-aircraft machine-guns, and mortars. A request was made by the Serbian Territorial Defence that the weapons be handed over and the fighters would be guaranteed peace and security; however, Mr. Alajbegovic, the leader of the Muslim units, refused and continued with the provocations. The Territorial Defence command made a decision to carry out an attack on the Muslim strongholds in Muslim villages; however, the Serbs from the neighbouring hamlets warned the Muslims and they withdrew. When the Serbian Territorial Defence entered Madjer village, Fejzo Hurko was captured along with his wife and son and taken to Novica Andric's village and told to go to the garage next to his house. They were provided with shelter so that nothing would happen to them. They only stayed there for 15 to 20 minutes before they were taken to the school centre to be housed. During the period of time that they spent in the garage, nobody maltreated them or tortured them. Novica Andric is aware that his father, Miodrag, was captured by the Muslims on his way home from work and taken to prison. He was then sentenced to 20 years in prison for the alleged killings of the three Muslims and the alleged incident in the garage. He was acquitted after the successful appeal. In relation to the secondary school centre, Novica Andric was aware that this was a holding centre for all families leaving the town centre, both Muslims and Serb families stayed there together. As Novica Andric passed the centre, he saw between 25 to 30 men playing five-a-side football. Novica Andric was re-called to the line of defence as a driver, and in the course of his job he visited Rasadnik detention facility. He has no knowledge that detainees were subjected to physical torture whilst staying at the facility. Both Serbs and Muslim detainees were held at Rasadnik. During his first few visits to the facility he personally saw that the detainees were given the same food that the detention facility staff and the soldiers of the brigade ate. He was aware that the detainees kept cows for food and assisted in chopping wood for working -- and working in the barn. And that would be the summary, and as you decided I would like to call these photo -- did I understand well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before doing so. Yes, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I know that Karadzic's summary is not evidence, but he said that case against witness's father included incident in the garage, but judgement that will be in evidence is not included in that judgement, only the crime of killing civilians in this village Bjelogorci in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, do you agree with Mr. Zec's comment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that Mico Andric, the father of Novica Andric, was accused and sentenced for the garage, but later on he was acquitted. However, I have not studied the judgement. I'll ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: After having seen the photo, why don't we take a look at the judgement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to call up ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court 1D12014. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what this photograph shows and when it was taken?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: The photograph was taken during the reconstruction of what happened in the village of Bjelogorci. This is the garage where false witnesses said that they had been mistreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any significant changes in terms of what this garage looks like compared to the time about which these witnesses testified?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No changes. There was just a regular garage door, and the garage was used and is used to this day as a summer kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did that happen? What time did they mention?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: End of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: End of May?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: End of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that time was the summer kitchen already being used?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were they served anything and where was that prepared?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: They were served coffee in this summer kitchen that was there then and is there to this day, and they were kept there only for 15 hours [as interpreted] until vehicles came from Rogatica which is 5 kilometres away from the village.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12015, could we please have that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just, could you remind me of the time of reconstruction, Mr. Andric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The time of reconstruction was the month of May or June, I think. They were roughly trying to look at the period when that had actually happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What year, Mr. Andric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was 1999, 8 or 9 before the acquittal, the judgement of acquittal. All international institutions were present there, all institutions that were present in Bosnia and Herzegovina then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As the witness testified, if there were no serious changes, you can skip the photos and move on to your next topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whose false testimony was not accepted? Which testimony was rejected when your father was acquitted?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Omanovic Hamdija's testimony was rejected and Hamdija's brother's testimony and Sefik Hurko, father's name Fejzo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. When you speak, could you kindly speak to the microphone so that the interpreters could hear you well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, let us just clarify this: Which person by the last name of Hurko testified and whose testimony was rejected?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Sefik Hurko, he gave false testimony and the cantonal court in Sarajevo assessed that these were false statements and that resulted in the judgement of acquittal later, the one that is presented here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about his father, did he testify?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: His father testified in Sarajevo, over there. He did not testify at this trial of Miodrag Andric, and their statements differed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which one of the two was in the garage during those 20 minutes?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Hurko Sefik, Hurko Fejzo, and Fejzo's wife. That was very brief, until the vehicle came for them, Ljubomir Cerovic, the then-assistant for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you help us clarify this: Your father, was he accused for the garage and was the garage included in this judgement of acquittal?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had been convicted because of the alleged garage and the alleged killing of civilians. After the reconstruction and after the witnesses were heard again, it was proven that the testimony provided had been false.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what does the judgement of acquittal refer to?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: The garage and the killing of three civilians, the alleged killing of three civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Trial Chamber is satisfied, I have no further questions at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I asked you to check with the -- if the judgement refers to the garage part as well. Is there a way to check it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. President, I'm reading it as we speak and it appears to have dealing with the three -- the killing of three civilians, but I'm not all the way through it, but the -- in the findings themselves he's actually acquitted of the killings of three civilians. I don't see any reference to the garage in the findings, but I'm in the process of looking at the statement of reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you agree with Mr. Zec?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: So far as I've been able to see, yes. I think that this could be a subject of cross-examination since the witness has given testimony on this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But given that Mr. Karadzic made that presentation, I'd like to hear confirmation that he agrees with Mr. Zec. Otherwise he has to go to -- go through the judgement and tell us what part refers to garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it's an 18-page judgement, so would you like to take maybe a five- or ten-minute break so he can read it and satisfy himself what the situation is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has no difficulty with it, but it will go to the Defence time. The Chamber will rise for five minutes. --- Break taken at 9.27 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Karadzic, have you done the reading?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and we have established what it's about. Can we call up D3043 in e-court, please, the basic court decision of the cantonal court in Sarajevo. Can we look at the following page, please. In the statement of reasons -- and this is the third page in English - in the statement of reasons it says that, it's the fifth or the sixth line, it says: "... the Deputy Cantonal Prosecutor partially modified the indictment at the hearing by indicting the accused Miodrag Andric for the same crime with a partially modified factual description ..." and so on and so forth. Can we now look at page 8 in e-court, please. It's Serbian page 5 and the English page 8. "Sefik Hurko...," here this is the second paragraph in the middle: "Sefik Hurko stated that he was held captive in the garage of the accused ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Andric, are you able to tell us if your father was sentenced for the garage by the lower court?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, because you overlapped with the interpretation, you were not heard by the interpreters. Please repeat your answer and in the future please put a pause before you start answering the question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Throughout the trial the garage was mentioned and that was part of the whole case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know in what sense the prosecutor or how the prosecutor amended the indictment during the process?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked him whether he knew. I didn't ask him to speculate. It says here that it was amended and there is no evidence that he was convicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic invites the witness to comment what prosecutor in that case was changing in the indictment or whatever changes he made. That's just not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I understood the question to be asking the witness whether he knew whether the prosecutor -- the indictment had been amended. I think the witness can answer. Yes, if you can answer, Mr. Andric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that they dropped the garage in the amendment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Excellencies, the lower court does not mention it as a part of the conviction, so that's why it was not mentioned in the appeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, was your father found guilty of anything?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that's it for your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As for the objection to the judgement, it's a fact that he was not convicted for the garage in the lower court decision, so that's why there was no mention of it by the Defence or the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. As you have noted, Mr. Andric, your evidence in chief in this case has been admitted in writing, i.e., through your statement in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you will be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Andric.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I think it's already clear, but let me ask you first a couple of background questions. Your father's name is Miodrag Andric, also known as Mico; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your family house is in the village of Kosovo, Rogatica municipality; this is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Next to your family house is the garage where Sefik Hurko, Fejzo Hurko, Izeta Hurko, and Abdulah Hurko were held on or about 14 August 1992. This is correct? Is it correct that these people were held?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No. It was like this: They were in the garage. They were not detained there. They were staying there. The garage was not locked while they were there, and Sefik, Fejzo Hurko -- Sefik Hurko, Fejzo Hurko, and his wife, Izeta, were there, the three of them. The fourth person was not there, the fourth person that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Abdulah Hurko is missing since, so I take it you don't know anything about his whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No, the fourth person was not brought there. That person was not there. I don't know whether that person died during the counter-attack of the forces that were up there. I'm not going into that. These three people, however, were brought to the garage. They were not locked in there. The garage was open throughout that whole time and they stayed there briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Among the soldiers who held the Hurko family members were Stojan Perkovic; Brane Krsmanovic; Dragomir Abazovic, also known as Pidje; Danko Neric; and Rajko Kusic. This is correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: There was a number of persons, Rajko Kusic, Stojan Perkovic, Krsmanovic, Abazovic; that's it. They did not detain them. They were talking to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The Hurko family members were held in your garage against their will and they were not allowed to leave; this is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I notice an issue of translation. You are saying "being held," and witness is rebutting or answering "they were not detained."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I have noted the same issue, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please bear that in mind. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, can you answer my last question or do I have to repeat?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The Hurko family members, they were held in your garage against their will and they were not allowed to leave, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: They were not being held after being captured, after the counter-attack by the Serbian forces. A pistol and two boxes of bullets of 70 pieces each were found on them, so they were armed during capture and they were taken to Rogatica. They were placed there to prevent -- among the soldiers there were already people -- those people whose relatives had died. So it was a move to prevent some kind of revenge on them. So they were sheltered there until the vehicle arrived that was going to take them to Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, I notice that you're repeating a lot of facts that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me intervene. The question was, Mr. Andric, whether they were allowed to leave when they stayed in your garage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were allowed to leave, but they had nowhere to go because the village was already under attack. They were safer there than in the zone of -- in the combat zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Back to you, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Sefik, Fejzo, and Abdulah, they were beaten and tortured by the soldiers who held them in your garage; this is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No. I said that this fourth person, Abdulah, was not brought to the garage at all. Throughout that whole time when they were there, I was present and I state with certainty that there was no abuse or mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: In 2009 Stojan Perkovic pled guilty before the court of BiH to crimes committed in Rogatica, including those committed in your garage; do you know this?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I know that he's serving his sentence, but I don't know what acts he was sentenced for.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The judgement is in evidence in this case, and it is D01665. But, Mr. Andric, the reality is that Stojan Perkovic pled guilty to and was convicted of this crime that you say never happened; right?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: There was no mistreatment. I don't know what he admitted to in the indictment or of being charged with. I'm not aware that there was any mistreatment in that garage. There is only one truth. I don't know of any other truth, and the truth is as I stated. I'm ready to take the lie-detector test or any other test. If the side that is giving false statements is also prepared to submit themselves to the same test, then we will see what the outcome is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Just to be clear, I take that you're aware that Sefik Hurko was held in your garage again the day after, which would be 15th August 1992. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No. After he was taken away then he did not return to the garage anymore. These are false statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You told us that you were a driver policeman in the military police of the Rogatica Brigade. Commander of the brigade was Rajko Kusic; this is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Ljubomir Cerovic that you referred to in your statement, he was head of the security and intelligence department until 30th November 1992, when he lost his life. After Cerovic it was Zoran Carkic who became new head of the security and intelligence department; this is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your immediate superior in the military police unit was Radenko Ilic, was he?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You told us in your statement that you had visited Rasadnik several times in the course of your duties. It is correct, isn't it, that Muslim civilians were detained at Rasadnik, including old people and women?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Other than Rasadnik and the military detention, there was the reception centre located in the secondary school centre. So it was closed later, but they were not detained -- the centre closed once the school began to operate, so they were not detained in the same place where these other military prisoners were held but in a facility next to it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We cannot distinguish -- no, your words were not interpreted at all, you just overlapped while the interpretation was going on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. In line 2, the witness said that besides the military detention there was also a reception centre which was relocated from the school once the school began to work. [In English] Not located in, relocated from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 24479.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, in front of you there will be a list of war prisoners sent by the Drina Corps command to the command of the 4th Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade and to Lieutenant-Colonel Cerovic 1st February 1993. If you look at the title of the document, there is a reference to Vili. This Chamber has received evidence that "Vili" is a nickname of Vinko Bojic who was warden of Rasadnik. In other words, Vili, the Vili camp, is Rasadnik; this is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: It's not a camp. It was a reception centre up there. As far as the military remand prison is concerned, it was called the military remand prison or detention unit. Nobody called it Rasadnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: My question was: The Vili camp is referenced here in this document. This is Rasadnik; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: That camp - in fact, not camp but centre - was called Rasadnik, not Vili.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does the word in B/C/S "logoru" mean "camp"? Yes, Mr. Zec? Can I hear from the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes it does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 2 it was said, "Nobody called Rasadnik Vili." Line 2 on page 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Aha. Did you say that? Do you confirm that, Mr. Andric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. What Mr. Karadzic has just said, you told us that Rasadnik was never called as Vili. Do you confirm having said that, Mr. Andric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Do you accept -- do you confirm that Vinko Bojic was also known as Vili and Vinko Bojic was warden of Rasadnik? Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Well, let's have a look at this list of names --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I referred earlier to P03267, page 7, when I said that you received evidence about Vinko Bojic and his nickname Vili.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Andric, if you look at the list of names, there's a name of Edina Musovic under item number 1. Edina is a Muslim female name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Edina was born in 1972. Under item number 2 there's a name Biba Kustura. Biba is a Muslim female name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Biba was born in 1928. Under number 3 is Nura Kustura. Nura is a Muslim female name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Nura was born in 1930. Under item number 4 it says here Hanua Kustura. This name also appears in another document that I'm going to show to you after. It says there Hanuma Kustura, with m. Hanuma is an old-fashioned Muslim name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And Hanuma was born in 1892, which means that at the time of her detention at Vili's, or Rasadnik, she was 101 years old, Mr. Andric, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: According to this, yes, but I had no insight into who was there because it was not my job to go into those buildings. My job was to deal with soldiers who somehow violated military discipline. I cannot confirm who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I just read to you first four names, all female names. In fact, they appear all the way down to number 17 as well as the name item 41, next page on this list. The reality is, Mr. Andric, that the Muslim civilians were detained at Rasadnik, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Items 32 to 35 on this list are the name of Sefik Hurko, Mahir Jasarevic, Fejzo Hurko, and Alija Isakovic, whose statements you have reviewed and they all say they were detained in Rasadnik; this is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6155, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can I have P06153.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, in front of you there will be a list of detained persons dated 10 April, 1993. This list was sent by the Drina Corps command Lieutenant-Colonel Slobodan Cerovic, who we saw a moment ago as a receiver of this previous list. Here Cerovic sends a list of detainees to the command of the East Bosnia Corps and to the Ministry of Justice and Administration, Slobodan Aviljas. The names of Muslim civilians that I read to you from the previous list also appear on this list. Can you see them?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mahir Jasarevic, who I also mentioned, is item 32 which should be next page on this list. Let's have a look at something that you have already seen in the statement of Mahir Jasarevic. It's ID07602, in it page 4. Mahir said that sometimes in summer 1993 Vinko Bojic, Zoran Carkic, and you, Novica Andric, packed him and other prisoners into a bus, including a pregnant woman, and took them to Zvornik. Mr. Andric, the civilians were detained at Rasadnik and you know this because you drove a group of them to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: That is correct. That group was supposed to go to the Muslim territory because they had expressed their wish to go behind the lines to the territory controlled by the army of their people. Muslim authorities obstructed that agreement to move them to the territory under their control, and I believe after a day or two they were returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just -- do you agree that they were detained in Rasadnik before they were transferred to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was at the same time a reception centre up there, the one that was moved from the school. Maybe there were some of them who were moved from the school. I don't know about all the people who were there. I did not go inside to be able to confirm, and I didn't know all these people personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: We are talking about the people that you drove to Zvornik. They were detained in Rasadnik, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mahir also said in his statement, same page, page 4, that women, children, and old people from Satorovici, Berkovici, and other villages in Rogatica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: -- were detained at Rasadnik --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you want to upload the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: We can, Mr. President. It's ID07602, page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And Mahir said there that women, children, and old people from Satorovici, Berkovici, and other villages in Rogatica were detained at Rasadnik. He said that two -- that two old women from Berkovici - Nura, age 102, and Aisa, aged 100 - died after one year of detention. This is what was happening at Rasadnik, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. It's possible, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Well, we can then call P0152 -- sorry, P06152 which is exhumation report dated 4 November 1998, and I'll be looking at the part with -- should be English page 9, B/C/S page 7. And that part of the exhumation report refers to Rasadnik. And according to this report, 14 bodies of 14 people were found exhumed from this location, from Rasadnik. And item number 11 is Hanka Kustura, born 1895. Item 12, Sejfo Mirvic, 1948. Next page is Aisa Osmanovic, born 1898, which means that she was 95 in 1993. Halil Vatres born in 1928. So the reality is, Mr. Andric, that a number of civilians died at Rasadnik as a result of the severe conditions they were subjected to, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, because as I said I came very rarely to Rasadnik. I'm not aware of all the things that went on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: At the end of your statement you referred to the events after the fall of Zepa in 1995. You talked about Ahmet Brgulja. Let me ask you first about Avdo Palic. You know who Avdo Palic was?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The VRS captured Avdo Palic after the fall of Zepa and he was held in an apartment in Rogatica; this is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The apartment was used by Zoran Carkic, which, in fact, belonged to a Muslim from Rogatica; this is also correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You provided guards for the apartment. You brought Danko Frganja, Goran Ristanovic, and Slobodan Obrenovic to keep Palic there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: They were brought to be with him while he stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Following the orders issued by the VRS Main Staff on 10 August 1995, you, Mr. Andric, and Zoran Carkic drove Avdo Palic from Rogatica to a prison called Mlin near Bijeljina, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: The name of prison was not caught by --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: It's Mlin. It's M-l-i-n. Mlin, near Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: So you drove Palic from Rogatica to Mlin, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 24641.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: In front of you there will be an order issued by Ljubisa Beara on 10 August 1995. In paragraph 1 it refers to Atlantida to be transferred to Mlin, Bijeljina. Paragraph 2 says that Captain Carkic arranged this with Major Kusic and personally carry out the task by announcing his arrival to Colonel Todorovic in the IBK and so on. Mr. Andric, this is the order, this one on the screen. This is the order pursuant to which you and Carkic drove Palic to Mlin, and Atlantida is Avdo Palic; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know what it's called, but it's true that we drove him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the order of the VRS Main Staff; this is also correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6156, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The reason for driving Palic to Mlin and keeping him in the apartment before that was to hide him from public and the ICRC, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Keeping him in that apartment, he was provided better conditions than other prisoners because he was a high-ranking officer. That was the reason. But he was removed because there were troops whose family members were killed in the attack at Bubanj Potok by forces led by Avdo Palic. There was a fear that the families might do something to him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the transcript, line 23, a better translation would be "sheltered," not "removed." And I don't think Bubanj Potok was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The body of Avdo Palic was exhumed from a mass grave in Vragolovi which is 10 kilometres from the Rogatica town. You know this, do you?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, who did it? Who took Palic back from Mlin, kill him, and buried him at Vragolovi?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I turned over Avdo Palic in Bijeljina and I don't know what happened later. There's probably documentation as to who took him over there. My role in this was the trip from Rogatica to Bijeljina and leaving him in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Let's focus now to Ahmet Brgulja. Ahmet did not reach --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could we take a look at the map, Rogatica, Mlin, and the mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Can we have 65 ter 19145. Mr. President, this is a map from our court binder, and if we can zoom middle where these triangles are.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Andric, can you see the triangle first from the bottom. It says "the garage of Novica Andric." Can you confirm this is approximate location of your family house? Then above you will be able to see "Rogatica town" if you look at the map.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And to the left side from "Rogatica town" there is a star and it says "Vragolovi mosque," and above that it says "Vragolovi."

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And also above that on the right side it says "Rasadnik Farm." Can you confirm these are approximate locations of the -- of these locations that I just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about Mlin, Mlin prison?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Yes, before that I would like to tender this map and I will call another map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is not in evidence yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll -- any objection, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6157, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have P04675.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll not broadcast this. But why is it under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I wasn't able to check that and thank you for reminding me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think I know why, but it's related to intercepts, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we please zoom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we could find a better one -- yes, but let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President, are you satisfied that you've found Vragolovi and Mlin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, Mlin is near Bijeljina; correct? The prison Mlin that you took Palic to, that's near Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: It is specifically in Bijeljina, in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And in this map you see Bijeljina on the right side?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we scroll down. Still down.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And on the bottom of the map do you see Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So how far is Mlin from Rogatica, roughly? Is it more than 100 kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 200 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Let's focus now to Ahmet Brgulja. Ahmet did not reach Kladanj, as you suggested. He was detained at Rasadnik, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I saw him at Boksanica. He was going in the direction of Kladanj. I think he left. I don't know if and when he returned from there. I saw him at Boksanica, as I stated, with the convoys on their way to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have D02133.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, in front of you will be a list of Muslim prisoners compiled by Zoran Carkic with whom you drove Palic to Mlin. This list was authorised by Zdravko Tolimir. It says: "Starting on 28th July 1995, the following citizens of Muslim ethnicity were accommodated at military reception centre in Rogatica." This military reception centre is Rasadnik; this is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Under items 1, 2, and 3 are the names of Zepa leaders, Mehmed Hajric, Hamdija Torlak, and Amir Imamovic. Under item 17, next page, is Ahmet Brgulja who you saw in Boksanica; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Under 45 it says Atlantida, 1958, is in a different location, safe location. This was Avdo Palic that you and Carkic held in the apartment; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Andric.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much do you have for your re-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fifteen to 20 minutes, perhaps shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we'll take a break now for half an hour. We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you allow me another two minutes, because the issue is the case of this witness's father, Miodrag Andric. And as you remember, there was an issue what was included in that case. And Mr. Karadzic argued it was the garage incident was involved in that case, and Mr. Karadzic argued on page 12 on today's transcript that the prosecutor amended the indictment and that the garage was dropped. Mr. Witness agreed to that. So I have indictment. It's 65 ter 24688. So that's all I would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So could you put that to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't -- we have it in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: We have it in e-court but we don't have translation unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, do you see on the first page the name of your father, Miodrag Andric, also known as Mico?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This is the indictment against your father. It's 6 September 1996. Do you confirm this is the indictment pursuant to which your father was tried in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: So I would kindly ask you to slowly read words after it says, "Dana 03 June 1996 ..." It says "1996," I believe it should say "1992," but nevertheless can you slowly read this paragraph -- or rather, I'm sorry, perhaps you can read it for yourself and tell us whether -- what charges are here, what incidents.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: This has to do with charges concerning the killing of three civilians; however, I believe that he had an amended indictment --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: -- in which the garage was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This is the indictment pursuant to which your father was tried and judgement reflects this indictment. There is no garage. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the question is whether this is the indictment which had been modified or -- your case is that this is the initial indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Correct and the only indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So could you ask that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Seems that he claims that the indictment was modified. I say it's not, so I don't know -- I can ask again but he will give the same answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you could later on prove that the initial date of indictment brought against Miodrag -- Mr. Miodrag Andric.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President, it should be in the judgement pursuant to which indictment his father was tried and whether it was modified or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Andric, do you confirm that 6th of September, 1996, was the date on which your father was prosecuted for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not September, June. The time of the killing, actually, that's June. I don't understand why witness Sefik Hurko was heard during the trial if my father had not been charged with the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Again, that's the matter of the proceedings and it's all explained in the judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, for your reference judgement is -- I have 1D0 -- ID12018. This is the first-instance judgement, and at page 2 in the reasoning it refers to this indictment of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's take a look. What page?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: So in B/C/S it should be page 2. Can we -- page -- English page 2 as well see. Page 3 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, can you see this judgement? This is the first-instance judgement against your father. This one is from 1997 and in the reasoning it says: Senior public prosecutor under investigation number 6 September 1996 indicted Miodrag Andric, and so on. So the indictment that I showed to you a moment ago is the indictment pursuant to which your father was tried; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender the indictment which is 65 ter 24688.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P6158, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Andric, now that we're on the subject of this document, the latest one, please take a look at this statement of reasons. It says in line 5 or 6 and the deputy cantonal prosecutor partially modified the indictment at the hearing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: We are back to the same position that I was objecting at the beginning of this issue with the judgement. Mr. Karadzic asking the witness to comment the legal proceedings in Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: It's clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- you didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I can see where it's going. It's again about this minor modification of indictment which has nothing to do with dropping charges is the core of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We haven't heard the question. Yes, please carry on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Andric, this indictment that was shown to you dated the 9th of September, 1996, that was used as a basis, was it modified, amended, during these proceedings? And to what extent was the garage spoken about during the trial?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Throughout the trial garage -- the garage was talked about and witnesses were heard about the garage, and that is to say that the accused person was charged with the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the idea underlying the reconstruction of the garage?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: The reconstruction of the scene established that witnesses provided false testimony. In the first statement given in Sarajevo, the witness actually claimed that there was a small door on the garage, and then when they came to the actual spot and when they took a photograph of the garage then he changed his statement. So he basically adjusted his statement to what suited him, but basically this testimony, these statements, were false.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who carried out this reconstruction of the garage?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: The entire reconstruction was carried out by the cantonal prosecutor's office, the MUP of the canton of Sarajevo, the MUP of Republika Srpska, the OHR ombudsman, and the Human Rights Institution were all present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Andric. I'd like to ask you something: These lists that were shown to you, these lists of these persons that were called captured persons here, are they accurate or not? Did you know how reliable these lists were?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about all of it. I don't know who all the persons there were. Basically I don't have much information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 18 of today's transcript, in lines 14 and 15, the learned Mr. Zec said to you, presented information as to the following: That Mr. Cerovic lost his life on the 30th of November, 1992. Did you know him personally, and is it true that that is when he lost his life?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: That is correct. He lost his life on that day. A planted anti-tank -- anti-armour mine killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any explanation as to -- was this an important event? Did the brigade and corps know about that? Were they informed of the fact that Cerovic had been killed?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Cerovic an important person in the military structure?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: He was assistant commander for security in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like us to take a look at P6155 briefly. What was Mr. Cerovic's rank?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: He was a captain or a major. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the date. How is it possible that on the 1st of February, 1993, the Drina Corps is sending information to him three or four months after he was killed?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Perhaps we can see last page of this document because I was talking about - and witness confirmed - about Ljubomir Cerovic, who was security officer. It's -- I'm sorry, it's the first page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: It's about Slobodan. If I'm not mistaken, it's Slobodan Cerovic. It's another person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or lieutenant -- who was lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Exactly and different rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure we are seeing "Slobodan."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: That's another list -- not this one list. The other list which was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we can ask, yes. Thank you, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now take a look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Actually, did you have two Cerovic's in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No, one Cerovic was in the brigade and this other one was in the corps, the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this fourth, that pertains to Rogatica, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have a look at who this Slobodan is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Because of overlapping, the interpreters didn't hear the witness's answer. What did you say, Mr. Andric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Rogatica Brigade, the 1st Podrinje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the -- what position did Mr. Cerovic was in the Drina Corps? Who was in the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Slobodan Cerovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know exactly. At any rate, this man did exist, I mean in the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not possible that the Cerovic, Slobodan Cerovic, who was in the Drina Corps coincidentally stayed in the Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade? That's why this message was sent to him when he was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we briefly take a look at P6153. Slobodan Aviljas, does that name ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you take a look at this list and can you see whether it was sent to Slobodan Aviljas?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I apologise. This is the list that I was referring to earlier and this was sent by Slobodan Cerovic, Lieutenant-Colonel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I think he's coming to that. Why don't we see the last page. Yes, we see assistant commander Lieutenant-Colonel Slobodan Cerovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And we were also talking about Ljubomir Cerovic who was security officer, so two different people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So do you confirm, Mr. Andric, now that this is sent by Slobodan Cerovic, who was the assistant commander in the Drina Corps and whose rank was a lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was your role in the transfer of Lieutenant-Colonel Palic to Mlin?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I was a driver in the military police, so I did that driving along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever give a statement anywhere about that?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I gave a statement at the crime police administration in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they trust you and how did you prove that you were telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, lie-detector tests were carried out and it was established that the statements were truthful, as they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Today on page 22 and then page 23, when a rather complex question was put to you, your answer was "yes." So please do help us establish what this "yes" refers to. I'm going to read it out in English so that you receive a better translation: [In English] "Q. I just read here you first four names, all female names. In fact, they appear all the way down to number 17 as well as the name item 41, next page on this list. The reality is, Mr. Andric, that the Muslim civilians were detained at Rasadnik, isn't it?" The answer is: "Yes." [Interpretation] Can you tell us whether you confirmed that these persons were at the detention unit in Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: They were there at the reception centre. They were right next to each other. Basically they were at the reception centre there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it says, further on, 32 to 35, I'm going to read it out in English again: [In English] "... are the names of Sefik Hurko, Mahir Jasarevic, Fejzo Hurko and Alija Isakovic, whose statements you have referred and they all say they were detained in Rasadnik; this is correct, isn't it?" [Interpretation] Now you said "yes." What is correct, that you read that or that you know that these persons were detained in Rasadnik in that part?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Sefik Hurko, Izeta Hurko, Fejzo Hurko, and Alija Isakovic were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, because of your overlapping, they didn't hear the answer of the witness. Can you repeat your answer. Sefik Hurko, Izeta Hurko and Fejzo Hurko were what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in military detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And on page 23 -- actually, before that, can you tell us on which basis they were in military detention and the others were at the reception centre?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, since the two Hurkos had pistols and two boxes with 70 bullets, they were considered to be armed persons and that's why they were brought into military detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When were they taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: That happened after the counter-attack because the Muslim units from the village of Madjer torched the village of Dobromirovici and Lelek. Then in the counter-attack Fejzo's wife and Fejzo Hurko and Sefik Hurko were taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And they were in your garage. Were they your prisoners or your family's prisoners or whose prisoners?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: They were prisoners of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Over here on page 23 -- I'm going to read it out to you in English: [In English] "Mr. Andric, the civilians were detained at Rasadnik and you know this because you drove a group of them to Zvornik." [Interpretation] Your answer: [In English] "That is correct. That group was supposed to go to the Muslim territory ...," [Interpretation] and so on. This part "it is correct," what does it refer to? Does it refer to the fact that you drove them or to the fact that they were prisoners in Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No, they were at this reception centre and that means that they expressed a wish to temporarily change their place of residence in order to go to the territory that was under the control of their people; however, the Muslim authorities did not allow that. They allowed them to enter the area of Tuzla, but after that they obstructed that and then they returned them to Rasadnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have the map, P6157.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'd like to ask you to explain to all of us who held what under their control so that all the participants, primarily the Trial Chamber, would get a proper picture as to who controlled what.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think this was an issue in direct or cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To understand the location probably I think it's relevant who held what -- what territory -- what places on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: But that's something that -- perhaps you want to hear that, but that's something that he was supposed to put in his direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us see. Please carry on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in a bit in order to see most of the central part of the municipality. And I kindly ask the usher to help Mr. Andric with the electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's zoom in further. Is it sufficient, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, please, could you tell us, for example, who by the end of the summer of 1992, during those critical days before Rogatica was liberated by the Serbs, where was the separation line? Who held what and could you put an S on the Serb side and an M on the Muslim side and tell us who held what.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it's -- your question is of such a general nature, how is it relevant? How does it arise from the cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic? Unless it has specific bearing on the location of school or the garage -- location of Mr. Andric's house and Vragolovi.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Excellency, that was mentioned. Vragolovi, well let's see who controlled Vragolovi, who could have destroyed the mosque there. Who was where in that area so that we can understand what it was that the Serbs held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think to the mosque -- yes, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And the Vragolovi issue came in relation to exhumation of Avdo Palic, that's the place where he was exhumed. There was no question about Vragolovi in 1992, either in direct or in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who was in control of Vragolovi in 1995 may be relevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Excellencies, all these markings could be of relevance, otherwise why wouldn't the Prosecutor then submit a neutral map without any markings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably they couldn't find a better one in the time-frame. Then you can move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And would you permit me to ask the witness to draw a line between the Muslim-held and the Serb-held areas in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But how does it arise from the line of cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The garage and the fighting and the capture of those people on the list occurred in 1992, so I want to put to the witness what the situation was in the villages from which these people were placed in the reception centres. Why were elderly people in the reception centres. Why were they not in their own villages? This does arise from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please proceed. Could you draw a line, Mr. Andric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This line is the line that goes along the village of Kosovo towards the direction of Leleci. I think the houses of Leleci is not -- are not shown here. Madjeri was under the control of the Muslim forces, Madjeri, Kozici, Kopljevici. There was a line of defence straight through the village --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear which village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- between the Muslim and the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please draw the lines along the whole municipality, indicating who was where, if you're able to do that; if not, that's all right.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know everything in detail. In any case, the Muslim forces were already holding the areas around the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then can you please circle the villages that were held by the Muslims. Who held Vrazalice?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please circle that and place an M next to that.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about Bulozi?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's to the south of Vrazalice, Bulozi.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: That was also under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Otricevo?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: M.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Brcigovo?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: M.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Lubardici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it goes beyond the scope you suggested. So the area below that line belonged to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you put the date of today, which is 28th of February, and your signature on the top of this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive as the next -- as next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3046, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, now I'm going to read out these villages, so I would like to ask you where there was combat or around which villages there was combat and around which ones there was no combat. In the document that talks about -- it's this one, P6153 and 6155. These documents talk about these persons who were in the Rasadnik reception centre. Were there any -- was there any fighting around the village of Zakomo?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Jasenica?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let's take it slowly, take a break. Jasenica?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dumonjici?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just make a break, please. Berkovici?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Kukavice?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Radava?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How are they relevant to the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, it was said here and also the heading can help us draw the conclusion that we're talking about prisoners, but the witness confirmed that these were civilians who were received at the reception centre. So what I am interested in is why would civilians be in the reception centre? Were these combat zones or were they ethnically cleansed? This is a very relevant question, both for the Defence as well as in terms of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Only to say for the record that the document says that these people were war prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you object to the line of re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I objected earlier and I thought that you want to hear this evidence, so I don't object anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we think you exhausted this issue. Please move on to your next topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at 65 ter 24439.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked about your role in the transfer of Avdo Palic from Rogatica to Mlin. 24439, 65 ter. In what capacity were you questioned at the B&H MUP in 1994? Is this the document?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, I was interviewed in my capacity as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at page 3 of the document, please. And page 4 in the English. I'm going to read this sentence: "According to my recollection, the above-mentioned Palic was with the mentioned guards for some ten days or so and in this time-period I brought them food two or three times ..." And then the conclusion at the bottom before your signature is: "I don't know anything about the fate of Avdo Palic." Was this statement tested on a lie-detector machine?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.
